title: Learning to say no ｜ 学会说"不"

sents.en: Not doing something will always be faster than doing it.
sents.cn: 不去做某事，永远比去做它更快。

sents.en: This philosophy applies in many areas of life.
sents.cn: 这一理念适用于生活的诸多方面。

sents.en: For example, there is no meeting that goes faster than not having a meeting at all.
sents.cn: 例如，没有什么会议比根本不开会进行得更快。

sents.en: This is not to say you should never attend another meeting, but the truth is that we say "yes" to too many things we don't actually want to do.
sents.cn: 这并不是说你永远不该参加任何会议，但事实是，我们对太多自己其实并不想做的事说了"好"。

sents.en: How often do people ask you to do something and you just reply, "Sure." Three days later, you're overwhelmed by how much is on your to-do list.
sents.cn: 人们多久会请你做件事，而你只是回一句"没问题"？三天后，你被待办清单上的海量任务压得喘不过气。

sents.en: We become frustrated by our obligations even though we were the ones who said "yes" to them in the first place.
sents.cn: 我们为自己的种种义务感到沮丧，尽管最初说"好"的正是我们自己。

sents.en: Even worse, people will occasionally fight to do things that waste time.
sents.cn: 更糟的是，人们偶尔还会争着去做浪费时间的事。

sents.en: You don't have to do something just because it exists.
sents.cn: 一件事存在，并不等于你就非做不可。

sents.en: It's worth asking if things are necessary.
sents.cn: 值得问问这些事是否必要。

sents.en: Many of them are not, and a simple "no" will be more productive than whatever work the most efficient person can cope with.
sents.cn: 其中许多并不必要，一句简单的"不"，比最高效的人能应付的任何工作都更富成效。

sents.en: But if the benefits of saying "no" are so obvious, then why do we say "yes" so often?
sents.cn: 但如果说"不"的好处如此明显，我们为何还如此频繁地说"好"？

sents.en: We say "yes" to many requests not because we want to do them, but because we don't want to be seen as rude or unhelpful.
sents.cn: 我们对许多请求说"好"，并非因为想做，而是因为不想显得无礼或不够帮忙。

sents.en: Often, we have to consider saying "no" to someone we will interact with again in the future·our co-worker, our spouse, our family and friends.
sents.cn: 通常，我们得考虑对将来还会打交道的人说"不"——同事、配偶、家人和朋友。

sents.en: Saying "no" to our superiors at work can be particularly difficult.
sents.cn: 对工作中的上级说"不"可能格外困难。

sents.en: In these situations, I like the approach recommended in Essentialism by Greg McKeown.
sents.cn: 在这种情况下，我偏爱《精要主义》一书中格雷格∙麦基翁所建议的方法。

sents.en: He writes, "Remind your superiors what you would be neglecting if you said 'yes' and force them to deal with the trade-off.
sents.cn: 他写道："提醒你的上级，如果你说'好'会疏于哪些事，迫使他们去面对这个取舍。

sents.en: For example, if your manager comes to you and asks you to do X, you can respond with 'Yes, I'm happy to make this the priority.
sents.cn: 例如，如果经理来找你，让你做X，你可以这样回应：'好啊，我很乐意把它作为优先项。

sents.en: Which of these other projects should I deprioritize to pay attention to this new project?'"
sents.cn: 那我该把其他哪个项目降优先级，好腾出精力做这个新项目？'"

sents.en: Collaborating with others is an important element of life.
sents.cn: 与他人协作是生活的重要一环。

sents.en: The thought of straining the relationship outweighs the commitment of our time and energy.
sents.cn: 一想到会损害这段关系，其分量便超过了我们在时间与精力上的付出。

sents.en: For this reason, it can be helpful to be gracious in your response.
sents.cn: 因此，回应时保持客气是有帮助的。

sents.en: Do whatever favors you can, and be warm-hearted and direct when you have to say no. But even after we have accounted for these social considerations, many of us still seem to do a poor job of managing the trade-off between yes and no. We find ourselves over-committed to things that don't meaningfully improve or support those around us, and certainly don't improve our own lives.
sents.cn: 尽你所能去帮忙，而在不得不拒绝时，则要热心而直接。但即便我们把这些社交因素都考虑进去了，许多人似乎仍不善于权衡"好"与"不"之间的取舍。我们发现自己过度承诺于那些并不能切实改善或支撑身边之人、当然也无益于自身生活的事情。

sents.en: Perhaps one issue is how we think about the meaning of yes and no. The words "yes" and "no" get so often used in comparison with each other that it feels like they carry equal weight in conversation.
sents.cn: 或许问题之一在于我们如何看待"好"与"不"的含义。"好"和"不"这两个词常被拿来相互比较，以至于在对话中仿佛分量相当。

sents.en: In reality, they're not just opposite in meaning, but of entirely different magnitudes in commitment.
sents.cn: 而现实中，它们不仅意思相反，在承诺的分量上也截然不同。

sents.en: When you say "no", you're only saying "no" to one option.
sents.cn: 当你说"不"时，你只是对某一个选项说"不"。

sents.en: When you say "yes", you're saying "no" to every other option.
sents.cn: 而当你说"好"时，你是对其他所有选项说"不"。

sents.en: I like how economist Tim Harford put it, "Every time we say 'yes' to a request, we're also saying 'no' to anything else we might accomplish with the time." Once you're committed to something, you've already decided how that future block of time will be spent.
sents.cn: 我欣赏经济学家蒂姆∙哈福德的说法："每次我们对一个请求说'好'，我们同时也对用这段时间本可完成的任何其他事说'不'。"一旦你承诺了某事，就等于已经决定了未来那段时间块将如何度过。

sents.en: In other words, saying "no" saves you time in the future. Saying "yes" costs you time in the future.
sents.cn: 换言之，说"不"是为未来节省时间，说"好"则是耗费未来时间。

sents.en: "No" is a form of time credit. You retain the ability to spend your future time however you want.
sents.cn: "不"是一种时间信用，你保留了按自己意愿支配未来时间的能力；

sents.en: "Yes" is a form of time debt. You have to pay back your commitment at some point.
sents.cn: "好"是一种时间债务，你终须在某一刻偿还这份承诺。

sents.en: "No" is a decision. "Yes" is a responsibility.
sents.cn: "不"是一个决定，"好"是一份责任。

sents.en: Saying "no" is sometimes seen as a luxury that only those in power can afford.
sents.cn: 说"不"有时被视为一种奢侈，只有掌权者才负担得起。

sents.en: And it's true; turning down opportunities is easier when you can fall back on the safety net provided by power, money, and authority.
sents.cn: 这话没错——当你能依靠权力、金钱与权威所提供的保障网时，拒绝机会确实更容易。

sents.en: But it's also true that saying "no" is not merely a privilege reserved for the successful. It's also a strategy that can help you become successful.
sents.cn: 但同样没错的是，说"不"并非成功者独有的特权，它也是一种能助你成功的策略。

sents.en: Saying "no" is an important skill to develop at any stage of your career because it retains the most important asset in life: your time.
sents.cn: 说"不"是在职业生涯任何阶段都该培养的重要技能，因为它保住了生命中最宝贵的资产：你的时间。

sents.en: As investor Pedro Sorrentino put it, "If you don't guard your time, people will steal it from you." You need to say "no" to whatever isn't leading you toward your goals.
sents.cn: 正如投资人佩德罗∙索伦蒂诺所言："如果你不守护自己的时间，别人就会从你身上偷走它。"凡是不能带你走向目标的事，你都需要说"不"。

sents.en: Nobody embodied this idea better than Steve Jobs, who said, "People think focus means saying 'yes' to the thing you've got to focus on.
sents.cn: 没有人比史蒂夫∙乔布斯更能体现这一理念，他说："人们以为专注就是对必须专注的事说'好'。

sents.en: But that's not what it means at all.
sents.cn: 但那根本不是它的意思。

sents.en: It means saying 'no' to the hundred other good ideas that there are.
sents.cn: 它意味着对成百上千个其他好点子说'不'。

sents.en: You have to pick carefully." Jobs had another great quote about saying "no", "I'm actually as proud of the things we haven't done as the things I have done.
sents.cn: 你必须仔细挑选。"乔布斯还有一句关于说"不"的名言："其实，我们对没做过的事，和做过的事一样感到骄傲。

sents.en: Innovation is saying 'no' to 1,000 things."
sents.cn: 创新就是对一千件事说'不'。"

sents.en: Over time, as you continue to improve and succeed, your strategy needs to change.
sents.cn: 随着时间推移，你不断进步并取得成功，你的策略也需要改变。

sents.en: The opportunity cost of your time increases as you become more successful.
sents.cn: 你越成功，时间的机会成本就越高。

sents.en: At first, you just eliminate the obvious distractions and explore the rest.
sents.cn: 起初，你只需剔除明显的干扰，去探索其余。

sents.en: As your skills improve and you learn to separate what works from what doesn't, you have to continually increase your threshold for saying "yes".
sents.cn: 随着技能提升，你学会区分何为有效、何为无效，就必须不断提高说"好"的门槛。

sents.en: You still need to say "no" to distractions, but you also need to learn to say "no" to opportunities that were previously good uses of time, so you can make space for better uses of time.
sents.cn: 你仍需对干扰说"不"，但也得学会对曾经是好时间用途的机会说"不"，好为更好的时间用途腾出空间。

sents.en: It's a good problem to have, but it can be a tough skill to master.
sents.cn: 这是个不错的问题，却也是一项难以掌握的技能。

sents.en: What is true about health is also true about productivity: an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.
sents.cn: 健康领域的真理，同样适用于效率：一分预防胜似十分治疗。

sents.en: More effort is wasted doing things that don't matter than is wasted doing things inefficiently.
sents.cn: 比起低效做事所浪费的精力，做无关紧要之事所浪费的更多。

sents.en: And if that is the case, elimination is a more useful skill than optimization.
sents.cn: 若果真如此，学会"剔除"便比"优化"更有用。

sents.en: I'm reminded of the famous Peter Drucker quote, "There is nothing so useless as doing efficiently that which should not be done at all."
sents.cn: 这让我想起彼得∙德鲁克的名言："没有什么比高效地去做根本不该做的事更无用。"
